title: Étale/pro-étale comparison intertwines scalar direct-image mates
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-quasi-separated-morphism], and let $a:A\to B$ be a homomorphism of discrete commutative rings. On the small étale and pro-étale sites use ordinary uncompleted derived categories of sheaves of modules over the constant ring sheaves [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf, def-weil-pbc-derived-categories, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations, def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Write $T_Z^{t}=B_Z\otimes^L_{A_Z}-$ for derived scalar extension on either site $t=\mathrm{et},\mathrm{proet}$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings], and $\nu_Z:Z_{\mathrm{proet}}\to Z_{\mathrm{et}}$ for the comparison morphism [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. Let $J\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ and assume $T_X^{\mathrm{et}}J\in D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},B)$.

For $R=A,B$ let $\beta^R_L:\nu_Y^*Rf^{\mathrm{et}}_{*,R}L\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf^{\mathrm{proet}}_{*,R}\nu_X^*L$ be the canonical comparison of [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison]. Let $\delta_{Z,L}:T_Z^{\mathrm{proet}}\nu_Z^*L\xrightarrow{\sim}\nu_Z^*T_Z^{\mathrm{et}}L$ be the canonical tensor comparison [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. On each site define $\gamma^t_L:T_Y^tRf^t_{*,A}L\to Rf^t_{*,B}T_X^tL$ as the adjoint transpose of $T_X^t(\varepsilon^A_L)$ after the canonical pullback/tensor identification, with $\varepsilon^A$ the counit of $f_A^*\dashv Rf_{*,A}$ [def-kun-projection-formula-map, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations, def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate]. Then the following is an equality of $B$-linear morphisms:
$$
Rf^{\mathrm{proet}}_{*,B}(\delta_{X,J})\circ\gamma^{\mathrm{proet}}_{\nu_X^*J}
=\beta^B_{T_X^{\mathrm{et}}J}\circ\nu_Y^*(\gamma^{\mathrm{et}}_J)\circ\delta_{Y,Rf^{\mathrm{et}}_{*,A}J}\circ T_Y^{\mathrm{proet}}((\beta^A_J)^{-1}).
$$
No invertibility of $\gamma^{\mathrm{et}}$ or $\gamma^{\mathrm{proet}}$ and no flatness of $B$ over $A$ is assumed.

proof.text: Consolidate the two canonical etale scalar/pullback definitions by reusing the published K-flat-normalized isomorphism. Prove that it equals the previous inverse scalar mate: iterated ordinary mates identify the ordinary reverse comparison; its scalar-unit equation holds degreewise; the exact localization square commutes with the geometric representative factors; the derived scalar adjunction gives the reverse normalization. Invert it and invoke uniqueness of the K-flat normalization. This is a complete compatibility proof and preserves the maps in the remaining steps.

Write $C_Z^R=\nu_Z^*$ over $R$, $l_R=f_{\mathrm{et},R}^*$, $p_R=f_{\mathrm{proet},R}^*$, $r_R=Rf_{\mathrm{et},*,R}$, $s_R=Rf_{\mathrm{proet},*,R}$, and $T_Z^e,T_Z^p$ for scalar extension. The adjunctions $l_R\dashv r_R$ and $p_R\dashv s_R$ are the canonical ordinary derived adjunctions [def-kun-projection-formula-map, def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Let $d_{R,M}:p_RC_Y^RM\xrightarrow{\sim}C_X^Rl_RM$ be the inverse-image square in [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison]. Its counit compatibility, read using the transpose formula [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], is
$$\varepsilon^p_{R,C_X^RL}\circ p_R(\beta^R_L)=C_X^R(\varepsilon^e_{R,L})\circ d_{R,r_RL}.$$
Here $\beta^A_J$ and $\beta^B_{T_X^eJ}$ are invertible: $f$ is qcqs, and $J$ and $T_X^eJ$ are bounded below by hypothesis. This invokes the arbitrary-discrete-ring theorem, rather than the finite-ring-only canonical-mate node.

source.place: Finite rings paragraph, canonical direct-image comparison and its counit normalization

proof.text:
Let $c^e_M:l_BT_Y^eM\xrightarrow{\sim}T_X^el_AM$ and $c^p_N:p_BT_Y^pN\xrightarrow{\sim}T_X^pp_AN$ be the pullback/scalar comparisons. Scalar extension is a derived ringed-topos pullback [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings]. The tensor-pullback theorem [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] supplies these comparisons and $\delta$. Use the canonical composition and 2-isomorphism normalization of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] for the commutative site square of [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison], with coefficient maps $A\to B$. Its ring maps commute because they all send a constant $a$ to its image in $B$. Consequently, on every $M\in D(Y_{\mathrm{et}},A)$,
$$\delta_{X,l_AM}\circ T_X^p(d_{A,M})\circ c^p_{C_Y^AM}=C_X^B(c^e_M)\circ d_{B,T_Y^eM}\circ p_B(\delta_{Y,M}).\tag{*}$$
Indeed both sides identify the same composite derived ringed pullbacks, starting at $p_BT_Y^pC_Y^AM$ and ending at $C_X^BT_X^el_AM$; the two paths through the site square give the specified 2-isomorphism. The cited normalization identifies their compositors and tensor comparisons. It applies to small sites in the common module universe and to arbitrary unbounded complexes and nonflat ring maps. Thus it does not require $T_Y^eM$ to be bounded below.

source.place: Finite rings paragraph, compatibility of site comparison with derived coefficient extension; Stacks 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), 0D6D (lemma-derived-pullback-composition)

proof.text:
Put $P=r_AJ$. Precompose the requested equality with the isomorphism $T_Y^p(\beta^A_J)$. It suffices to prove equality of the two maps
$$U=s_B(\delta_{X,J})\circ\gamma^p_{C_X^AJ}\circ T_Y^p(\beta^A_J),\qquad V=\beta^B_{T_X^eJ}\circ C_Y^B(\gamma^e_J)\circ\delta_{Y,P}$$
from $T_Y^pC_Y^AP$ to $s_BC_X^BT_X^eJ$. By [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate], the transpose of $\gamma^t_L$ is $T_X^t(\varepsilon^t_{A,L})\circ c^t_{Rf^t_{*,A}L}$, as stipulated in the statement. Naturality of the $B$-counit therefore gives the transpose of $U$ under $p_B\dashv s_B$ as
$$\delta_{X,J}\circ T_X^p(\varepsilon^p_{A,C_X^AJ})\circ c^p_{s_AC_X^AJ}\circ p_B(T_Y^p(\beta^A_J)).$$
Naturality of $c^p$ rewrites the last two factors as $T_X^p(p_A(\beta^A_J))\circ c^p_{C_Y^AP}$. Substituting the $A$-counit equation of Step 1 gives
$$U^\flat=\delta_{X,J}\circ T_X^p(C_X^A(\varepsilon^e_{A,J}))\circ T_X^p(d_{A,P})\circ c^p_{C_Y^AP}.$$

source.place: Formal properties and finite rings paragraphs: transpose the pro-etale coefficient comparison

proof.text:
Naturality of $\delta$ at $\varepsilon^e_{A,J}:l_AP\to J$ changes the first two factors from Step 3 to $C_X^B(T_X^e(\varepsilon^e_{A,J}))\circ\delta_{X,l_AP}$ [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback]. Apply equation $(*)$ at $M=P$. Thus
$$U^\flat=C_X^B\bigl(T_X^e(\varepsilon^e_{A,J})\circ c^e_P\bigr)\circ d_{B,T_Y^eP}\circ p_B(\delta_{Y,P}).$$
Every factor is a $B$-linear morphism: the tensor comparisons are ringed module pullbacks and the counit is a module counit. This computation uses no inverse for either coefficient mate.

source.place: Finite rings paragraph: explicit transport of the coefficient comparison using the tensor square

proof.text:
The transpose of $V$, using the $B$-counit equation in Step 1 with $L=T_X^eJ$, is
$$V^\flat=C_X^B(\varepsilon^e_{B,T_X^eJ})\circ d_{B,r_BT_X^eJ}\circ p_B(C_Y^B(\gamma^e_J))\circ p_B(\delta_{Y,P}).$$
Naturality of $d_B$ at $\gamma^e_J:T_Y^eP\to r_BT_X^eJ$ [sk-thm-pe-direct-image-comparison] rewrites this as
$$C_X^B\bigl(\varepsilon^e_{B,T_X^eJ}\circ l_B(\gamma^e_J)\bigr)\circ d_{B,T_Y^eP}\circ p_B(\delta_{Y,P}).$$
The defining transpose of $\gamma^e_J$ [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] replaces the parenthesis by $T_X^e(\varepsilon^e_{A,J})\circ c^e_P$. This equals Step 4. Injectivity of the adjunction Hom bijection gives $U=V$. Finally precompose with $T_Y^p((\beta^A_J)^{-1})$ to obtain exactly the displayed equality in the statement. Only the two hypothesized bounded-below inputs are needed for the invertible $\beta$ maps; the intermediate scalar extension $T_Y^eP$ may be unbounded.
